title: Identify Inactive Customers with Anti-Join
description_markdown: Find all customers who have NEVER placed an order using a `LEFT JOIN ... WHERE orders.order_id IS NULL`. Return `c.customer_id`, `c.first_name`, and `c.email`. Order by `c.customer_id`.
starter_query:
-- Anti-join with LEFT JOIN and IS NULL
SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.email
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE ...
solution_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.email FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL ORDER BY c.customer_id ASC;
solution_explanation: An anti-join filters for rows where the right side of the LEFT JOIN failed to produce any match (`o.order_id IS NULL`).
hints: Use `WHERE o.order_id IS NULL`.
Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.
Query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.email FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL ORDER BY c.customer_id ASC;

title: Detect Unsold Catalog Products via Anti-Join
description_markdown: Perform an anti-join from `products` to `order_items` on `product_id` using `LEFT JOIN ... WHERE oi.order_item_id IS NULL` to find products that have never been purchased. Return `p.product_id`, `p.product_name`, and `p.price`. Order by `p.product_id` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Anti-join products to order_items
SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.price
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
WHERE oi.order_item_id IS NULL
ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.price FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id WHERE oi.order_item_id IS NULL ORDER BY p.product_id ASC;
solution_explanation: An anti-join uses a LEFT JOIN combined with `WHERE right_table.pk IS NULL` to isolate unmatched left-table records.
common_mistakes: Checking IS NULL on a nullable right column rather than the primary key.
interview_tip: Always filter on the right table's PRIMARY KEY or NOT NULL column to ensure NULL indicates an absence of match.
hints: Join condition: `p.product_id = oi.product_id`.
Filter condition: `WHERE oi.order_item_id IS NULL`.
Query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.price FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id WHERE oi.order_item_id IS NULL ORDER BY p.product_id ASC;

Filter `WHERE a.assignment_id IS NULL`.

SELECT e.emp_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, e.job_title

WHERE sub.emp_id IS NULL

hints: Left join `sub` on `e.emp_id = sub.manager_id`.
Filter `WHERE sub.emp_id IS NULL`.

ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT parent.category_id, parent.category_name FROM categories parent LEFT JOIN categories sub ON parent.category_id = sub.parent_category_id WHERE sub.category_id IS NULL ORDER BY parent.category_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Surfaces terminal nodes in the category tree by checking for the absence of child rows.
common_mistakes: Reversing parent and child aliases.
interview_tip: In taxonomy models, products are typically attached only to leaf categories.

Filter `WHERE sub.category_id IS NULL`.

title: Find Active Catalog Products with Zero Orders
description_markdown: Perform an anti-join from `products` to `order_items` on `product_id`. Filter for active merchandise (`p.is_active = TRUE`) that has never been ordered (`oi.order_item_id IS NULL`). Return `p.product_id`, `p.product_name`, and `p.price`. Order by `p.product_id` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Anti-join on active products
SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.price
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
WHERE oi.order_item_id IS NULL AND p.is_active = TRUE
ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.price FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id WHERE oi.order_item_id IS NULL AND p.is_active = TRUE ORDER BY p.product_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Filters out discontinued/inactive items to focus purely on active products suffering from zero sales conversions.
common_mistakes: Placing p.is_active = TRUE in the ON clause which would retain inactive products.
interview_tip: Left-table filters belong in WHERE, not ON.
hints: Join `p.product_id = oi.product_id`.
Filter `WHERE oi.order_item_id IS NULL AND p.is_active = TRUE`.

Query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.price FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id WHERE oi.order_item_id IS NULL AND p.is_active = TRUE ORDER BY p.product_id ASC;

title: Identify Engineering Personnel with Zero Project Allocation
description_markdown: Join `employees` and `departments` on `dept_id` where `d.dept_name = 'Engineering'`. Anti-join to `assignments` on `e.emp_id = a.emp_id` (`a.assignment_id IS NULL`). Return `e.emp_id`, `e.first_name`, and `e.salary`. Order by `e.salary` descending, then `e.emp_id` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Anti-join with department filter
SELECT e.emp_id, e.first_name, e.salary
FROM employees e
JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id
LEFT JOIN assignments a ON e.emp_id = a.emp_id
WHERE d.dept_name = 'Engineering' AND a.assignment_id IS NULL
ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT e.emp_id, e.first_name, e.salary FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id LEFT JOIN assignments a ON e.emp_id = a.emp_id WHERE d.dept_name = 'Engineering' AND a.assignment_id IS NULL ORDER BY e.salary DESC, e.emp_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Combines an inner join for departmental filtering with an outer anti-join to detect unallocated technical personnel.
common_mistakes: Left-joining departments instead of inner-joining.
interview_tip: Mixing INNER JOIN (for filtering) and LEFT JOIN (for anti-join exclusion) is a standard production design.
hints: Join `d` on `e.dept_id = d.dept_id`, left join `a` on `e.emp_id = a.emp_id`.
Filter with `WHERE d.dept_name = 'Engineering' AND a.assignment_id IS NULL`.

Query: SELECT e.emp_id, e.first_name, e.salary FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id LEFT JOIN assignments a ON e.emp_id = a.emp_id WHERE d.dept_name = 'Engineering' AND a.assignment_id IS NULL ORDER BY e.salary DESC, e.emp_id ASC;

title: Identify Students with Zero Completed Course Records
description_markdown: Perform an anti-join from `students` to `enrollments` on `s.student_id = e.student_id AND e.status = 'completed'` where `e.enrollment_id IS NULL`. Return `s.student_id`, `s.first_name`, and `s.major`. Order by `s.student_id` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Anti-join with status filter in ON clause
SELECT s.student_id, s.first_name, s.major
FROM students s
LEFT JOIN enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id AND e.status = 'completed'
WHERE e.enrollment_id IS NULL
ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT s.student_id, s.first_name, s.major FROM students s LEFT JOIN enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id AND e.status = 'completed' WHERE e.enrollment_id IS NULL ORDER BY s.student_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Placing `e.status = 'completed'` in the ON clause treats any other enrollment status as a non-match, identifying students who have never finished any course.
common_mistakes: Putting `e.status = 'completed'` in WHERE, which would eliminate all non-matches.
interview_tip: In conditional anti-joins, the qualifying condition MUST be in the ON clause.
hints: Keep `AND e.status = 'completed'` inside the `ON` clause.
Filter `WHERE e.enrollment_id IS NULL`.

Query: SELECT s.student_id, s.first_name, s.major FROM students s LEFT JOIN enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id AND e.status = 'completed' WHERE e.enrollment_id IS NULL ORDER BY s.student_id ASC;

title: Implement Anti-Join Pattern Using NOT EXISTS
description_markdown: Use the `NOT EXISTS` correlated subquery pattern to find all customers who have NEVER placed an order. Return `c.customer_id`, `c.first_name`, and `c.email`. Order by `c.customer_id` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Anti-join using NOT EXISTS
SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.email
FROM customers c
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE ...
)
ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.email FROM customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE c.customer_id = o.customer_id) ORDER BY c.customer_id ASC;
solution_explanation: `NOT EXISTS` is semantically equivalent to a LEFT JOIN ... IS NULL anti-join, and often optimizes identically under modern query optimizers.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to correlate the subquery with `c.customer_id = o.customer_id`.
interview_tip: NOT EXISTS is NULL-safe: it never produces the 3-valued logic pitfalls associated with NOT IN.
hints: Use `WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE c.customer_id = o.customer_id)`.
Order by `c.customer_id ASC`.
Query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.email FROM customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE c.customer_id = o.customer_id) ORDER BY c.customer_id ASC;

title: Implement Safe Anti-Join Pattern Using NOT IN
description_markdown: Use the `NOT IN` subquery syntax to find departments that have no employees. Explicitly add `WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL` to the subquery to ensure three-valued logic safety. Return `d.dept_id` and `d.dept_name`. Order by `d.dept_id` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Safe NOT IN anti-join
SELECT d.dept_id, d.dept_name
FROM departments d
WHERE d.dept_id NOT IN (
  SELECT dept_id FROM employees WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL
)
ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT d.dept_id, d.dept_name FROM departments d WHERE d.dept_id NOT IN (SELECT dept_id FROM employees WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY d.dept_id ASC;
solution_explanation: If a subquery evaluated by `NOT IN` contains even a single NULL, the entire `NOT IN` expression evaluates to UNKNOWN (returning 0 rows). Adding `WHERE col IS NOT NULL` guarantees correctness.
common_mistakes: Omitting WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL in the NOT IN subquery.
interview_tip: This is one of the most famous SQL interview questions: why does NOT IN fail when the subquery returns NULL?
hints: Use `WHERE d.dept_id NOT IN (SELECT dept_id FROM employees WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL)`.
Order by `d.dept_id ASC`.
Query: SELECT d.dept_id, d.dept_name FROM departments d WHERE d.dept_id NOT IN (SELECT dept_id FROM employees WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY d.dept_id ASC;

title: Identify Enrolled Students with Zero Graded Marks
description_markdown: Find enrolled students who have NO graded mark records across any of their course enrollments. Join `students` and `enrollments` on `student_id`, then anti-join to `marks` on `e.enrollment_id = m.enrollment_id` (`m.mark_id IS NULL`). Group by `s.student_id`, `s.first_name`, and `s.last_name`. Return `s.student_id`, `s.first_name`, and `s.last_name`. Order by `s.student_id` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Multi-table anti-join to marks
SELECT s.student_id, s.first_name, s.last_name
FROM students s
JOIN enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id
LEFT JOIN marks m ON e.enrollment_id = m.enrollment_id
WHERE m.mark_id IS NULL
GROUP BY ...
ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT s.student_id, s.first_name, s.last_name FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id LEFT JOIN marks m ON e.enrollment_id = m.enrollment_id WHERE m.mark_id IS NULL GROUP BY s.student_id, s.first_name, s.last_name ORDER BY s.student_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Detects active enrollments that have not received any test scores.
common_mistakes: Leaving off GROUP BY, resulting in duplicate student rows if multiple enrollments lack marks.
interview_tip: Grouping eliminates duplicate parent rows produced by intermediate 1-to-many bridge tables.
hints: Join `s` to `e`, left join `e` to `m`.
Filter `WHERE m.mark_id IS NULL` and group by the student keys.

Query: SELECT s.student_id, s.first_name, s.last_name FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON s.student_id = e.student_id LEFT JOIN marks m ON e.enrollment_id = m.enrollment_id WHERE m.mark_id IS NULL GROUP BY s.student_id, s.first_name, s.last_name ORDER BY s.student_id ASC;

SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.total_amount

LEFT JOIN payments pay ON o.order_id = pay.order_id

ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.total_amount FROM orders o LEFT JOIN payments pay ON o.order_id = pay.order_id WHERE pay.payment_id IS NULL ORDER BY o.order_id ASC;

Filter `WHERE pay.payment_id IS NULL`.

title: Identify Courses with No Final Exam Assessment
description_markdown: Find courses where NO student has ever taken a final exam assessment (`m.assessment_type = 'final'`). Use an anti-join or `NOT EXISTS`. Return `c.course_id`, `c.course_code`, and `c.course_name`. Order by `c.course_id` ascending.
starter_query:

SELECT c.course_id, c.course_code, c.course_name

solution_query: SELECT c.course_id, c.course_code, c.course_name FROM courses c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM enrollments e JOIN marks m ON e.enrollment_id = m.enrollment_id WHERE e.course_id = c.course_id AND m.assessment_type = 'final') ORDER BY c.course_id ASC;
solution_explanation: NOT EXISTS with a joined subquery safely checks across multiple tables for the complete absence of a matching record.
common_mistakes: Allowing courses with midterms but no finals to be omitted.
interview_tip: NOT EXISTS handles multi-table condition checking elegantly without creating wide outer joins.
hints: Use `NOT EXISTS` with `enrollments` joined to `marks`.
Check `e.course_id = c.course_id AND m.assessment_type = 'final'`.

Query: SELECT c.course_id, c.course_code, c.course_name FROM courses c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM enrollments e JOIN marks m ON e.enrollment_id = m.enrollment_id WHERE e.course_id = c.course_id AND m.assessment_type = 'final') ORDER BY c.course_id ASC;

title: Find Customers Who Have Never Purchased an Electronic Product
description_markdown: Use `NOT EXISTS` to find customers who have NEVER ordered any product in the 'Electronics' parent category or its child categories (e.g., category_id IN (1, 2, 3, 4)). Return `c.customer_id`, `c.first_name`, and `c.email`. Order by `c.customer_id` ascending.
starter_query:
-- NOT EXISTS anti-join for electronics category
SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.email
FROM customers c
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM orders o
  JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
  WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND p.category_id IN (1, 2, 3, 4)
)
ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.email FROM customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND p.category_id IN (1, 2, 3, 4)) ORDER BY c.customer_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Combines 3 joined tables inside a correlated NOT EXISTS subquery to exclude customers with any purchase matching specific category criteria.
common_mistakes: Writing a simple NOT IN on orders without traversing to products.
interview_tip: NOT EXISTS with deep subquery joins is ideal for complex categorical exclusion queries.
hints: Use `WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND p.category_id IN (1, 2, 3, 4))`.

title: Identify Students with Zero Dropped Course Enrollments

solution_query: SELECT s.student_id, s.first_name, s.gpa FROM students s WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM enrollments e WHERE s.student_id = e.student_id AND e.status = 'dropped') ORDER BY s.student_id ASC;

Query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.email FROM customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND oi.discount > 0.00) ORDER BY c.customer_id ASC;

title: Find Departments with Zero Employees Earning at Least 150k
description_markdown: Use `NOT EXISTS` to find departments that have NO employees earning a salary of 150,000 or greater. Return `d.dept_id`, `d.dept_name`, and `d.budget`. Order by `d.dept_id` ascending.

FROM departments d
WHERE NOT EXISTS (

  WHERE d.dept_id = e.dept_id AND e.salary >= 150000
)
ORDER BY ...;
solution_query: SELECT d.dept_id, d.dept_name, d.budget FROM departments d WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM employees e WHERE d.dept_id = e.dept_id AND e.salary >= 150000) ORDER BY d.dept_id ASC;

title: Identify Professors Whose Students Have No Completed Grades

WHERE NOT EXISTS (

  JOIN enrollments e ON c.course_id = e.course_id
  JOIN marks m ON e.enrollment_id = m.enrollment_id
  WHERE c.professor_id = p.professor_id

solution_query: SELECT p.professor_id, p.last_name, p.department FROM professors p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM courses c JOIN enrollments e ON c.course_id = e.course_id JOIN marks m ON e.enrollment_id = m.enrollment_id WHERE c.professor_id = p.professor_id) ORDER BY p.professor_id ASC;
